                                                                            Abstract                                                 questions that span a hierarchical spectrum—from quali-
                                                                                                                                     tative relational reasoning to quantitative metric and kine-
                                         While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have                                         matic understanding. Evaluations reveal that the perfor-
                                         achieved impressive performance on semantic tasks, their                                    mance gains observed in structured indoor benchmarks
                                         spatial intelligence—crucial for robust and grounded AI                                     vanish in open-world settings. Further analysis using syn-
                                         systems—remains underdeveloped. Existing benchmarks                                         thetic abnormal scenes and blinding tests confirms that cur-
                                         fall short of diagnosing this limitation: they either fo-                                   rent MLLMs depend heavily on linguistic priors instead
                                         cus on overly simplified qualitative reasoning or rely on                                   of grounded visual reasoning. Our benchmark thus pro-
                                         domain-specific indoor data, constrained by the lack of                                     vides a principled platform for diagnosing these limitations
                                         outdoor datasets with verifiable metric ground truth. To                                    and advancing physically grounded spatial intelligence.
                                         bridge this gap, we introduce a large-scale benchmark                                       Project page: https://mingrui-wu.github.io/
                                         built from pedestrian-perspective videos captured with syn-                                 openbench/
                                         chronized stereo cameras, LiDAR, and IMU/GPS sensors.                                       1. Introduction
                                         This dataset provides metrically precise 3D information,
                                         enabling the automatic generation of spatial reasoning                                      Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) [2, 3, 6, 14,
                                                                                                                                     26, 28, 33, 42, 44, 57, 58, 60, 76] have emerged as pivotal
                                            * Corresponding author.                                                                  tools for interpreting and reasoning about the visual world,

• A benchmark and dataset for spatial intelligence.                                                          of the task hierarchy and representative examples at each
  We introduce OpenBench, a metrically precise outdoor                                                       level. The hierarchy begins with Relational Reasoning
  benchmark built from multi-sensor pedestrian-view data,                                                    (relative distance, relative direction, and qualitative ego-
  with 8,736 question-answer pairs. We will also release                                                     motion), which assesses a model’s foundational ability to
  additional raw multimodal videos.                                                                          form a qualitative, non-metric spatial representation of the
• Comprehensive evaluation of state-of-the-art (SoTA)                                                        scene. The second tier, Metric Reasoning, comprising ob-
  MLLMs. We conduct an extensive analysis of leading                                                         ject localization, absolute distance, and depth-aware count-
  open- and closed-source models, offering the first unified                                                 ing, introduces a more demanding challenge: grounding vi-
  assessment of spatial reasoning across static, relational,                                                 sual perception in an absolute metric scale to enable pre-
  and dynamic tasks under real-world conditions.                                                             cise, quantitative estimation of static properties like dis-
• Current spatial intelligence is fragile. Our findings re-                                                  tance. Finally, Kinematic Reasoning includes tasks such
  veal that existing MLLMs lack generalizable spatial intel-                                                 as absolute displacement and speed estimation. These re-
  ligence—their gains on indoor benchmarks do not trans-                                                     quire maintaining spatio-temporal consistency by tracking
  fer to open-world settings.                                                                                entities over time and understanding metric measurements
                                                                                                             and temporal intervals to compute dynamic quantities.
2. Benchmark                                                                                                 2.2. Data collection
2.1. Overview                                                                                                Platform. Our customized data collection platform, shown
Unlike previous works [37, 65] that primarily repurpose off-                                                 in the upper left of Fig. 3, is equipped with a stereo RGB
the-shelf datasets, OpenBench first establishes a purpose-                                                   camera system, a 32-beam LiDAR, and an IMU/GPS unit,
built data foundation through a customized multi-sensor                                                      all of which provide timestamp-synchronized data streams.
data collection effort that provides metrically-sound ground                                                 To ensure smooth motion, the platform is mounted on a
truth. Second, we designed a pipeline that extracts spatial                                                  manual cart navigated by walking operators.
information and generates question-answer pairs covering                                                     Data Processing and Curation. Our collection resulted in
the full spectrum of spatial intelligence, finalized by a care-                                              terabytes of raw data, which were then processed to gener-
ful human curation phase to ensure benchmark quality.                                                        ate a multimodal dataset. First, stereo images, point clouds,
   The tasks in OpenBench are structured as a hierarchy                                                      and IMU/GPS data were extracted with timestamps and
of three tiers, representing a progression of spatial reason-                                                carefully calibrated. Then LiDAR points were projected
ing capabilities. Fig. 2 provides a detailed breakdown                                                       to generate sparse depth maps. At last, all sequences were

Scene Selection. Our scene selection strategy is designed to                MLLM first identifies objects and generates textual descrip-
ensure environmental diversity while maintaining a strictly                 tions, which guide detection and segmentation models to
pedestrian-centric perspective, not road-centric. To this end,              produce pixel-level masks. These masks are temporally
our data collection spans a wide range of sites, including                  tracked using a point-tracking model (e.g., CoTracker [31])
university campuses, public parks, open plazas, and histori-                for motion consistency. Each object’s 3D point cloud is
cal sites. This pedestrian-centric perspective of open-world                subsequently reconstructed from depth maps and registered
scenes, rarely represented in current MLLM evaluations,                     in the world coordinate system using the estimated cam-
not only provides a critical complement to the field but also               era pose. Consequently, every object is represented by a
fulfills our objective of challenging linguistic priors in such             structured spatio-temporal profile that combines a detailed
unstructured environments. Please refer to Sec. B in the                    caption with a continuous 3D trajectory.
supplementary material for details of data collection.                      Stage 3: QA Generation and Curation
2.3. Benchmark Construction                                                 Finally, we convert the extracted structured spatio-temporal
                                                                            information into the final, high-quality video-QA bench-
We design a three-stage pipeline that transforms raw multi-
                                                                            mark. Specifically, we first resolve object ambiguity in
modal data into question–answer pairs. The stages include:
                                                                            open-world scenes (e.g., multiple identical street lamps)
(1) Data Preprocessing, (2) Spatial Information Extraction,
                                                                            by assigning each queried object a unique numerical ID,
and (3) QA Generation and Curation. An overview of the
                                                                            which is overlaid as a visual tag that consistently tracks
entire pipeline is illustrated in Fig. 3. Please refer to Sec. C
                                                                            the object throughout the video. All metric quantities (e.g.,
in the supplementary material for more details and Sec. D
                                                                            distance, speed) are then computed directly from the ob-
for an error analysis of this pipeline.
                                                                            jects’ spatio-temporal coordinates. Using these annotations,
Stage 1: Data Preprocessing                                                 we generate QA pairs through a template-based approach.
This initial stage transforms the raw multimodal recordings                 The automatically generated QA pairs are subsequently re-
into a structured format for analysis. First, the data is seg-              fined via an MLLM-assisted, human-in-the-loop curation
mented into shorter video clips, with all streams aligned                   process. From this curated pool, we sample 1,000 video
by their timestamps. From this synchronized data, we                        clips and nearly 1,000 verified QA pairs for each of the nine
generate two streams of geometric metadata: 1) a metric-                    tasks, ensuring balanced coverage across the three reason-
scale camera pose for each frame is estimated using ORB-                    ing tiers. The resulting benchmark, OpenBench, comprises
SLAM3 [11] from stereo images and IMU data, and 2) a                        8,736 high-quality QA pairs in total.
sparse depth map is created by projecting the calibrated Li-
DAR point clouds onto the image plane. At last, we sample                   3. Evaluation
keyframes at a fixed interval from each clip and bundle them                3.1. Evaluation Setup
with their corresponding camera poses and depth maps.
This process yields the metadata-enriched keyframes that                    Benchmark Models. We evaluate a broad spectrum of
serve as the primary input for the subsequent stage.                        MLLMs across various architectures and scales, covering
                                                                            both leading proprietary and publicly available models. All
Stage 2: Spatial Information Extraction                                     experiments are conducted using the VLMEvalKit [21] to

5.1. Multimodal Large Language Models                                 diversity and lack coverage of open-world and pedestrian-
Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) represent a                  centric settings. Such bias makes it difficult to assess gen-
significant advancement, extending the capabilities of Large          uine improvements in spatial reasoning. Moreover, current
Language Models (LLMs) [19, 28, 59] to jointly interpret              benchmarks often test recognition and retrieval rather than
and synthesize information across heterogeneous modal-                higher-order reasoning about spatial composition, causality,
ities [71]. The evolution of MLLMs from foundational                  or physical consistency—key aspects of spatial AI.
methods like CLIP [44] and BLIP-2 [34, 35], to pivotal

architectures interfacing visual features with frozen LLMs

and scene understanding [4, 43].                                      from pedestrian-perspective videos with precise geometric
    Despite this impressive progress, these foundational              supervision, it enables realistic assessment beyond indoor
MLLMs continue to face significant challenges in visual-              or synthetic datasets. Our findings expose a structural gap
spatial reasoning [38]. A strong reliance on textual priors           between today’s MLLMs and the level of spatial under-
often suppresses fine-grained spatial cues [23]. This issue           standing required for physically grounded AI. They further
is exacerbated by the lack of compositional training data             suggest that scaling visual encoders or expanding training
specifically designed to foster robust spatial intelligence.          corpora alone is insufficient; genuine progress will require
    Separate from these foundational models, there is also a          mechanisms capable of inferring, storing, and manipulating
growing body of work [10, 15, 16, 24, 62] focused on en-              3D geometric quantities in a principled manner.
hancing specific spatial reasoning capabilities. While these          Discussion. Our ablation studies point toward several
specialized models excel within their designated domains,             promising research avenues. Improving metric depth per-
they typically rely on task-specific training, auxiliary ge-          ception in open-world settings is essential, as this emerges
ometric inputs (e.g., depth maps, 3D reconstructions), or             as the principal bottleneck across spatial tasks. Integrating
explicit region-level supervision. As a result, their capa-           explicit geometric representations—whether through 3D-
bilities are closely tied to the training distribution and do         aware architectures, multi-view consistency, or hybrid sym-
not reflect the innate spatial understanding of a general-            bolic–neural reasoning—may help models move beyond
purpose model. Moreover, many such methods are built on               surface-level priors. Moreover, dynamic reasoning remains
static scenes, limiting their ability to reason about motion or       notably underexplored. Developing models that maintain
dynamic spatial relationships. In contrast, our benchmark             temporally consistent world models, reason over motion
evaluates the foundational spatial intelligence of general-           trajectories, and utilize sensor-derived ego-motion data rep-
purpose MLLMs without introducing new supervision or                  resents a critical next step.

                                                                3
    Captioner Prompt

    [Task]
    Your task is to analyze an image and output a JSON object containing lists of captions forstatic and dynamic objects.
    [Rules]
    1. Content Principle: Identify distinct physical objects. Each string in the lists must describe a **single entity**.
    Avoid plural or group descriptions (e.g., instead of “cars”, list “blue sedan”, “white SUV”).
    2. Ignore: Backgrounds (walls, roads), 2D elements (text, signs), minor parts of larger objects, natural or amorphous
    categories like “tree”, “bush”, “flowers”, “grass”, or “cloud”.
    3. Uniqueness: If an object has already been listed, do not list it again. Once no new unique objects can be found,
    STOP immediately and close the JSON list with a bracket.
    4. Classification: The identified objects should first be classified into static or dynamic.
    static objects: Stationary items. (e.g., a parked car, a bench, a trash bin).
    dynamic objects: Items visibly in motion. (e.g., a person walking, a car driving, a bird flying).
    5. Captions: All captions must be purely visual descriptions (e.g., “red sports car”, “person in yellow jacket”). Do
    not describe motion (e.g., avoid “person walking”).
    6. Empty Lists: If no objects of a certain type are found, use an empty list “[]”.

    [Example]
    {
        "static_objects": [
          "red sports car",
          "black street lamp",
          "green park bench"
        ],
        "dynamic_objects": [
          "man in blue jacket"
        ]
    }
    Your entire response must be a single, valid JSON object, strictly following the format shown in the ‘[example]‘. Do
    not add any other text.


                                          Figure 8. Prompt for the MLLM captioner.

Unlike benchmarks built upon existing, manually annotated           To ensure data fidelity, we conducted several independent
3D datasets [24, 37, 65], OpenBench employs a highly au-            calibration processes for all sensors and selected the optimal
tomated pipeline to extract spatial information and gener-          results. The quality of the stereo calibration can be mea-
ate QA pairs. While this automation enables scalability, it         sured by its reprojection error, which quantifies the distance
is crucial to analyze the potential sources of error. In this       between a detected pattern keypoint and its corresponding
section, we analyze these errors and demonstrate that they          point projected from the other camera view. Using a stan-
are minimal, and that the quality of OpenBench is ensured           dard chessboard pattern, our final selected calibration (from
through our rigorous calibration, validation, and curation          25 image pairs) achieved a mean reprojection error of 0.32
processes.                                                          pixels.


                                                                4
           Task                             Question Template
           Relative Distance                Measuring from the closest point of each object, which of the fol-
                                            lowing is closest to the {Q class}(id:{Q id}): {A class}(id:{A id}),
                                            {B class}(id:{B id}), {C class}(id:{C id}), or {D class}(id:{D id})?
           Relative Direction               If I am standing by the {C class}(id:{C id}) and facing the
                                            {A class}(id:{A id}), is the {B class}(id:{B id}) to my front-left,
                                            front-right, back-left, or back-right? The directions refer to the quad-
                                            rants of a Cartesian plane.
           Qualitative Ego-Motion           Assuming the video is recorded from a first-person perspective, which
                                            of the provided options best describes the person’s overall movement
                                            throughout the entire duration of the video? Choose from straight, left
                                            turn, right turn or U turn.
           Object 3D Localization           At approximately {T} seconds into the video, what is the Euclidean
                                            distance of the {A class}(id:{A id}) from the camera in meters?
           Absolute Distance                What’s the distance between the center of the {A class}(id:{A id}) and
                                            the {B class}(id:{B id}) in meters?
           Depth-aware Counting             At approximately {time sec}s, how many {class name}s are visible
                                            within {distance threshold} meters from the camera?
           Absolute Displacement            What is the displacement distance of the {A class}(id: {A id}) between
                                            {T1}s and {T2}s in meters?
           Absolute Speed                   What is the average speed of the {A class}(id: {A id}) between {T1}s
                                            and {T2}s in m/s?
           Quantitative Ego-Motion          How long has the camera travelled throughout the entire duration of the
                                            video in meters?

                                                                 7
Human Annotator Instructions
• Annotators are permitted unrestricted control over video playback. This includes the ability to play, pause, scrub
  the progress bar, and re-watch the video multiple times for each question to ensure their answer is as accurate as
  possible.
• The provided object captions (class names) may occasionally be imprecise. In cases of a conflict or discrepancy
  between the textual caption and the numerical ID tag shown in the video, the numerical ID should be considered
  the definitive ground truth. The object designated by the visual ID tag is the correct target for the question.
• For Numerical Answer (NA) tasks, provide the numerical value only, without any units (e.g., 12). For Multiple-
  Choice Answer (MCA) tasks, provide only the corresponding capital letter of the correct option (e.g., A).
• Before beginning the formal evaluation, annotators are provided with a calibration set. This set consists of 2 sample
  videos, their 20 corresponding question-answer pairs, and the associated ground truth (GT) answers. Annotators
  are instructed to review this material to familiarize themselves with the camera properties, the various question
  types, and to gain a reasonable sense of the metric scales used in the benchmark. This step ensures all annotators
  are properly calibrated before proceeding to the main evaluation tasks.


                                Figure 11. Human annotator instructions for evaluation.

       Component                       Content
       Question                        What’s the distance between the center of the {A class}(id: {A id})
                                       and the {B class}(id: {B id}) in meters?
       Formula post-prompt             In camera coordinates, x points right, y points down, and z points
                                       forward. To solve this, apply the following formula: Distance =
                                       ∥(R · p2 + T ) − p1 ∥. In this formula, p1 is the 3D position in the
                                       camera coordinate of first queried object observed at the earlier time t1 ,
                                       and p2 is the 3D position of second queried object observed in the cam-
                                       era coordinate at the later time t2 . The matrix R and vector T represent
                                       the rotation and translation the camera pose has changed at time t2 rel-
                                       ative to time t1 . If any piece of information required to use the formula
                                       is not present in the text, you must infer it from the video and then use
                                       it in the formula.
       Obj1 Info                       At {t1}s(t1 ) of the video, {B class}(id: {B id}) is located at p1 =
                                       [{p1 x},{p1 y},{p1 z}] meters relative to the camera.
       Obj2 Info                       At {t2}s(t2 ) of the video, {A class}(id: {A id}) is located at p2 =
                                       [{p2 x},{p2 y},{p2 z}] meters relative to the camera.
       Ego-motion Info                 Between {t1}s(t1 ) and {t2}s(t2 ), the camera’s relative translation is T =
                                       [{T x}, {T y}, {T z}] and the rotation matrix is R = [[{R11}, {R12},
                                       {R13}], [{R21}, {R22}, {R23}], [{R31}, {R32}, {R33}]].
       Setting                         Question Template
       Vanilla                         {Question} {Formula post-prompt}
       + One Localization(p1 )         {Obj1 Info} {Question} {Formula post-prompt}
       + Both Localization(p1 ,p2 )    {Obj1 Info} {Obj2 Info} {Question} {Formula post-prompt}
       + Ego-Motion(R, T )             {Ego-motion Info} {Question} {Formula post-prompt}
       + All(p1 , p2 , R, T )          {Obj1 Info} {Obj2 Info} {Ego-motion Info} {Question} {Formula
                                       post-prompt}
       + All(w/o Formula)              {Obj1 Info} {Obj2 Info} {Ego-motion Info} {Question}

                                Table 7. Templates for the Geometric Information Test.

                                                                    strained by model availability, two primary findings emerge
                                                                    from this data: (i) on OpenBench, the relationship between
                                                                    performance and model size is non-monotonic, often sat-
                                                                    urating or degrading; and (ii) the performance gain from
                                                                    newer generations on OpenBench is marginal, which stands
                                                                    in stark contrast to the significant and stable gains reported
                                                                    on VSI-Bench (e.g.>+23.0 for both families and all sizes).
                                                                       Our main paper’s analysis focuses on the comparison
                                                                    between OpenBench and VSI-Bench [65], as their shared
                                                                    video modality and tasks allow for a direct comparison. To
                                                                    validate that our findings regarding illusory progress on in-
                        (a) Normal scene.
                                                                    door benchmarks are not an artifact of VSI-Bench alone,
                                                                    we conducted an additional test on the multi-view indoor
                                                                    spatial benchmark, All-Angle-Bench [69]. The results in
                                                                    Tab. 13 confirm that the trend of performance gains from
                                                                    larger model scales and newer model generations persists on
                                                                    this benchmark as well. However, the magnitude of the gain
                                                                    from newer model generations is less significant than that
                                                                    observed on VSI-Bench. We hypothesize that this reduced
                                                                    gain may be due to the models’ lack of specific training for
                                                                    the multi-view data format required by All-Angle-Bench.

G. Privacy
To address privacy concerns, our data acquisition was con-
ducted exclusively in publicly accessible locations. Sub-
sequently, all collected data underwent a rigorous human
curation process to identify and remove any potentially sen-
sitive or private information.
